## Conceptual model generated

I wrote the conceptual model to `.wire/releases/01-data-foundation/design/conceptual_model.md`. It was checked automatically and passed 12 of 12 checks.

**Business rules check:** Wire recommends approved business rules before this step. The release has none, so I skipped the check using your reason ("business rules are out of scope for the foundation release"). The skip is recorded in `status.md` and in the execution log.

**What the model contains**

| Item | Count |
|------|-------|
| Business entities (things the business tracks) | 15, in 6 groups |
| Relationships between them | 18 |
| Open questions | 9 |

| Group | Entities |
|-------|----------|
| Customers | Customer, Address |
| Orders | Order, OrderLine, Product |
| Subscriptions | Subscription, SubscriptionEvent, CancellationReason |
| Payments | Payment, Invoice |
| Marketing | MarketingEvent, Campaign, WebSession |
| Fulfilment | Shipment, TrackingEvent |

The reporting outputs (MRR, churn, retention, lifetime value, attribution, on-time delivery) are listed as figures built from these entities, not as entities in their own right.

**Open questions:** all 9 must be answered before the model can be approved.

1. Are guest checkouts counted in revenue, and how are they linked to a customer?
2. Which system wins when Shopify and Stripe disagree on subscription status? (About 3% of subscriptions do.)
3. Does a paused subscription count as churn?
4. Which key joins Google Analytics visits to Stripe customers? The `user_id` field only exists from 2024.
5. The cancellation reason list still needs sign-off from Cathy Marsh. This blocks the build.
6. How are wholesale (B2B) customers treated in subscription reporting?
7. The source data has no address table, so we don't know where Address will come from.
8. Stripe has no key linking charges to invoices, which affects how refunds are netted off MRR.
9. Klaviyo campaign names and the free-text campaign names in Google Analytics may not match.

Questions 1 to 6 come from the requirements. Questions 7 to 9 are gaps found in the source data.

**Other changes**
- The release is now in the design phase.
- I changed one em-dash in the template's status line to a comma, to follow house style.

**Next step:** review the model with the business stakeholders. The 9 open questions need answers before it can be approved.
